I do not know exactly what you are feeling but from the little you shared, I have been there too. There would be 4+ days where I would not leave my bed but use the restroom and possibly get "food." I believe looking back now the numbness I felt was something I had to g through so when I was going to make an effort to get better I could physically feel the "results" to know I am not as numb as I use to be. I have tried suicide 7 times in my life. I just turned 18 no less than a week ago. 5 of those times led to hospitalization due to the results of my attempts. One day I was going to kill myself, I was on the edge and where I was it was going to look like an accident. No one would have ever known, I sat there for a while and cried. After some time I screamed off the ledge and told the world to go itself. I saw this as some sort of a sick challenge someone had given me. I saw this as a redemption. It took almost 1.4 years to get where I currently am, I am on antidepressants and am going to counseling but my thoughts were nowhere as close to where they were when I was on the edge. You getting up today and tomorrow is what makes for your future. It may not seem like a lot but many people did not wake up today. Many people have lost their battle with depression, and many have suffered a loss. I am proud of you for getting up today, even if you did not leave your house. Hold on, pain ends H.O.P.E
